strategy.summary: Commit 72802a9 ("Show each line's product name on an order") slowed GET /orders/:id: the detail scenario of perf/orders.js went from p95 22 ms to 32 ms and p99 23 ms to 33 ms, and a rerun confirmed it. The route now waits for productNames() as a third store round trip (6–9 ms each), one after the other with findOrder and orderLines. The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but they don't. The plan is to guard this with thresholds tagged to the detail scenario in perf/orders.js, set at the baseline plus 20%, then record and file the defect. The existing thresholds and scenarios stay as they are.
inScope: perf/orders.js detail scenario: p95 and p99 thresholds tagged {scenario:detail}, added beside the existing thresholds
Record the defect and file it on GitHub Issues
outOfScope: perf/search.js search p95/p99: the work item says these vary too much between good runs to judge (cv 64.4% / 12.8%), so they are noise and the script stays as it is
Speeding up the application (a person's work)
assumptions: Thresholds are the baseline medians plus the 20% headroom: p95 22 ms → p(95)<26.4, p99 23 ms → p(99)<27.6
The k6 scripts run against the real app at BASE_URL (http://localhost:4310); nothing is faked
The existing thresholds (http_req_failed rate<0.01, http_req_duration p(95)<2000) and both scenarios stay unchanged; the only change to the existing script is adding two threshold entries

defects.title: Order detail (GET /orders/:id) p95/p99 latency up ~45% since 72802a9 (extra sequential store round trip)
defects.description: AC1/AC2: in perf/orders.js the detail scenario should hold the last good runs' latency within 20%: p95 under 26.4 ms (baseline 22 ms) and p99 under 27.6 ms (baseline 23 ms). Actual: p95 32 ms (+46.2%, 31 ms on the rerun) and p99 33 ms (+43.6%, 32 ms on the rerun). The bisect's first slow commit is 72802a9 "Show each line's product name on an order". In it, src/app.js's /orders/:id route adds `await productNames(items.map(...))` after `await orderLines(order.id)`, and productNames in src/store.js makes its own roundTrip() (6–9 ms, ROUND_TRIP_MS 6 + jitter 3). The request now makes three store round trips one after another (findOrder, orderLines, productNames) instead of two, which adds about 7–10 ms per request. The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but the code fetches them in a separate second query. A possible fix: return each line's product name from orderLines, which already looks each product up for its priceCents, or otherwise avoid the extra round trip.
defects.evidence: k6 run perf/orders.js (full load, 20 req/s per scenario, 10s) at 35eaba9: http_req_duration{scenario:detail} ✗ 'p(95)<26.4' p(95)=31.27ms, ✗ 'p(99)<27.6' p(99)=33.47ms; k6 exit 99 "thresholds on metrics 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}' have been crossed". The list scenario and the existing thresholds pass.
